candidate_windows.window_text: Our baseline model is the BART Longformer encoder-decoder (BART-LED) of Beltagy et al. (2020). In all experiments, it has been first pretrained over the training set using the negative log-likelihood until convergence, which has typically set within 5 epochs, in line with what reported in Pasunuru et al. (2021). The best models on the validation set (average ROUGE) have then been finetuned with the reinforcement learning objectives in (2) and (4). BART-LED has 459M parameters, and the addition of the control variate for the RELAX experiments adds approximately 12M more parameters. We have used the Adam optimizer for training both the main BART-LED model and the parameters of the control variate of the RELAX gradient estimator. The learning rate of the main optimizer for the pre-training of the baseline has been set to the default of $3 \times 10^{-5}$ (Beltagy et al., 2020), before being reduced to $3 \times 10^{-6}$ for finetuning with the reinforcement learning approaches. For training the control variate, we have set an initial learning rate of $1 \times 10^{-2}$ and initialized the learnable $\log \tau$ parameter with a value of 0.5. The optimal size of the hidden layers of the control variate appears to empirically correlate with the maximum length of the reference summaries in the dataset. For Multi-News, we have set the size to be 256, and for WCEP to $40^{5}$ . For the multi-document coverage reward, we have used a $\beta$ value of 1.0. The entire model has been implemented on top of PyTorch Lightning<sup>6</sup>. Please refer to Table 5 for a full list of the hyperparameters. For all experiments, we have used an NVIDIA Quadro RTX 6000 with 24 GB of memory.
